description: a: every lemma family, Aasm fact and configuration abstraction the 5 KEVM claims depend on. Closed by `python3 pilot/tools/assemble_hard.py closure` (fails if a name grepped from the K sources or claims is missing here, or if an entry names something absent). Class T throughout. Loop/arith annotations: none (no claim contains a loop invariant or circularity; all paths are straight-line). Lean: none under variant A (no .lean in hard/certs).

annotations.statement: Every rule of K module BYTES-SIMPLIFICATION (lemmas/bytes-simplification.k) is a sound equation over the KEVM term algebra. Byte-array simplification lemmas (#buf/#range/#padToWidth/#asByteStack algebra). Rule bytes-simplification.k:282 `#padToWidth(32, #asByteStack(V)) => #buf(32, V) requires #rangeUInt(256, V)` is the fold the three getter return values need (Finding 0003b).
annotations.used_by_note: baked into the kompiled definition (main module LEMMAS-DRIVER) every claim is proved under, so the backend may apply any rule of the family to any claim; per-claim rule usage was not measured (no ablation run)
annotations.justification: Upstream KEVM lemmas (evm-semantics d4bf484a), all carrying [simplification]; the four Finding-0004 families were probed by 4 known-false identities (scripts/lemma-consistency.sh, none proved, on the laptop lemma definition). Not machine-checked against the semantics.

annotations.statement: The [simplification] rules that ship inside the stock KEVM EDSL closure (buf.md BUF, gas.md GAS-SIMPLIFICATION/INFINITE-GAS, hashed-locations.md HASHED-LOCATIONS) are sound. They are part of the KEVM verification substrate, not added by this bundle.
annotations.used_by_note: imported by EDSL, the base of LEMMAS-DRIVER
annotations.justification: Stock KEVM; trusted as part of semantics adequacy (A1).

annotations.statement: For the getter slot k (1 for vat, 2 for ilk, 3 for gem): #rangeUInt(256, #lookup(STORAGE, k)), i.e. the stored word is in [0, 2^256).
annotations.justification: SSTORE only ever writes a 256-bit word, so every storage cell of a reachable EVM state satisfies it; it is asserted in `requires`, not derived inside the claim (Finding 0003b caveat 1). Without it the #padToWidth fold does not fire.

annotations.statement: 0 <= ACCTID < 2^160 and 0 <= MSGSENDER < 2^160 (the executing account and the caller are 160-bit addresses).
annotations.justification: Every EVM account id and CALLER value is a 160-bit address by construction of the machine.

annotations.statement: <useGas> false </useGas>: the claims are proved with gas accounting switched off.
annotations.justification: Standard KEVM functional-correctness configuration. Consequence: every claim holds only for executions that do not run out of gas. Out-of-gas is an exceptional halt (status EVMC_OUT_OF_GAS, all gas consumed), which is neither the EVMC_SUCCESS of claims 01-03 nor the EVMC_REVERT of claims 04-05; no claim guarantees termination within any gas limit.

annotations.statement: <callStack> .List and <callValue> 0 and <static> false: GemJoin executes as the top-level frame of a non-static call with zero value, and its code runs under its own account (<id> = the account whose <storage> is constrained).
annotations.justification: Matches a direct external call. Not covered: execution via DELEGATECALL into GemJoin (then <id>/storage differ), STATICCALL (static=true), or a nested frame; R9 (callvalue > 0) is outside the claims.

annotations.statement: Pre conjunct #lookup(STORAGE, keccak(#buf(32, MSGSENDER) +Bytes #buf(32, 0))) ==Int 0 states wards[caller] == 0: the slot of key caller in the mapping at slot 0 under solc 0.5.12's layout keccak256(pad32(key) ++ pad32(slot)), with KEVM's keccak(Bytes) standing for Keccak-256.
annotations.justification: solc's documented mapping layout and KEVM's keccak hook (blockchain-k-plugin) computing Keccak-256 on concrete bytes. During the symbolic proof keccak stays an uninterpreted function and the proof needs neither injectivity nor a concrete value; the assumption only fixes what the Pre MEANS for the deployed contract.

annotations.statement: #rangeUInt(256, USR) and #rangeUInt(256, WAD): each ABI argument word of join's calldata is in [0, 2^256).
annotations.justification: A calldata word is 32 bytes, so every value it can hold is in range; #buf(32, X) is only the intended encoding for X in range. Excludes nothing a real call can send.
